content.text:
JPY and KRW invoices are now sent to the gateway in whole units, so ¥1,500 is charged as 1500. `npm test` passes (9 of 9).

**Root cause:** `buildChargePayload` in `src/payments/gateway/payload.js` lower-cases the currency code (`jpy`) for the gateway. It then passes that lower-case code to `toMinor`. The currency registry only had upper-case keys (`JPY`), so the lookup for `jpy` missed and fell back to a default of 2 decimal places. USD and EUR use 2 decimals anyway, which is why they were fine. Zero-decimal currencies (JPY, KRW, VND, CLP) were multiplied by 100. Three-decimal currencies (BHD, KWD) were also wrong, multiplied by 100 instead of 1000.

**Fix:** In `src/lib/currency/registry.js`, `exponent`, `isSupported` and `symbol` now look codes up case-insensitively through one helper. This fixes the gateway path and any other caller that passes a lower-case code.

**Tests:** I added three to `test/charge.test.js`: JPY 1500 → 1500, KRW 20000 → 20000, and a check that `exponent('jpy')` is 0 and `exponent('kwd')` is 3.

I only checked the charge path. Other callers (refunds, payouts, coupons, dunning) pass the stored upper-case code, so they were not affected. `src/legacy/money.js` multiplies by 100 unconditionally. I didn't check whether anything still uses it, so it's worth a look.

status_detail: JPY/KRW 100x overcharge fixed via case-insensitive lookup
